# Internationalization — nrscholar-frontend (web)

Languages: **English, Hindi, Gujarati** via `i18next` (`src/i18n.ts`). Translations are in `src/locales/{en,hi,gu}.json` under one `"translation"` namespace. The language is detected from `localStorage` (`i18nextLng`) and sent to the backend as `Accept-Language`.

- **[Preserve] Keys are `snake_case`** describing the text: `"select_language": "Select Language"`, `"parent_space": "Parent Space"`. Group related keys with a common prefix (`weekly_test_title`, `weekly_test_submit`).
- **[Standard] Every new or changed visible string uses `t()`.** That includes headings, buttons, placeholders, toasts, empty/error states and `aria-label`s. Only 15 of 59 screens use `useTranslation` today, so don't add more hardcoded English. When you touch a screen, translate the strings you change.
- **All three files change together**, with real Hindi (Devanagari) and Gujarati translations in a child-friendly tone. If unsure of a translation, add your best version and list it for review. Never leave a language missing (the fallback to English hides gaps).
- Interpolate: `t("xp_to_next_level", { xp })`. Never concatenate translated fragments. The brand name comes from the `{{brandName}}` default variable (set from `APP_CONFIG`). Don't hardcode "NR Scholar" in text.
- Learning content in `src/shared/assets/Content/` (NCERT) isn't UI text. Don't move it into locale files.
- Hindi and Gujarati strings are often longer, so check that layouts still fit at 360px.
